verdict.rationale: Supabase documents a first-party way to create a Supabase client for SSR frameworks like Next.js and SvelteKit, and offers a Next.js App Router template with cookie-based auth. That covers the framework-SDK part of the story. The evidence never describes middleware-based route protection or session verification at the edge; the JWKS URL is only a building block for that. Missing for 10: documented middleware for route protection, explicit edge-runtime session verification, coverage of peer frameworks beyond a brief mention, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can protect routes with first-party framework SDKs and middleware (Next.js and peers) that verify sessions at the edge

citations.quote: Create a Supabase client for SSR frameworks like Next.js and SvelteKit.
A Next.js App Router template configured with cookie-based auth using Supabase, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS.
